'''Iain Gordon''', [[Fellowship of the Royal Society of Edinburgh|FRSE]], is a mathematician, who is currently Professor of Mathematics, Vice-Principal and Head of the College of Science and Engineering at the [[University of Edinburgh]]. From the beginning of August 2026 he will take up a new position as Senior Vice-Principal at the [[University of Glasgow]]. His field of specialisation is representation theory and noncommutative algebra.

== Education and career ==

Gordon studied mathematics as an undergraduate at the [[University of Bristol]] (1991–94), took [[Part III of the Mathematical Tripos|Part III]] at [[Magdalene College, Cambridge|Magdalene College]], the [[University of Cambridge]] (1994–95), and completed his PhD on ''Representations of Quantised Function Algebras at Roots of Unity'' at the [[University of Glasgow]] under the supervision of Ken Brown (1995–1998). He was the [https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/school-of-mathematics/research/the-seggie-brown-bequest Seggie Brown Fellow] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210731020712/https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/school-of-mathematics/research/the-seggie-brown-bequest |date=31 July 2021 }} in Edinburgh (1998–99) and a postdoc at the [[Bielefeld University]], the [[University of Antwerp]] and [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|MSRI]] (1999–2000). He was a lecturer and then reader in the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of Glasgow]] (2000–2006), and since then has been the [[List of professorships at the University of Edinburgh|Professor of Mathematics at the University of Edinburgh]].

In 2005, Gordon was awarded the [[Berwick Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]] for his article ''Baby Verma modules for rational Cherednik algebras''.<ref>[https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/bulletin-of-the-london-mathematical-society/article/baby-verma-modules-for-rational-cherednik-algebras/16BACAF87511C8209C0AC364B74B01FE Baby Verma modules for rational Cherednik algebras]</ref> In 2008 he was awarded a 5-year EPSRC Leadership Fellowship to support his research on ''Rigid Structure in Noncommutative, Geometric and Combinatorial Problems''. In 2010 he was elected as a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] and was an [[List of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Hyderabad on ''Rational Cherednik Algebras''.<ref>[https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~igordon/pubs/RCA8.pdf Rational Cherednik Algebras]</ref> In 2014 he won the Edinburgh University Student Association's Van Heyningen Award for Teaching in Science and Engineering.<ref>[https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/school-of-mathematics/news?nid=345 Prof. Iain Gordon wins EUSA 2014 Teaching Award]</ref> Since 2018, he has been the Principal Investigator on a 6-year EPSRC Programme Grant with Arend Bayer, Tom Bridgeland, Agata Smoktunowicz and Michael Wemyss on ''Enhancing Representation Theory, Noncommutative Algebra and Geometry''. He was elected as Vice President of the [[London Mathematical Society]] in 2019.<ref>[https://www.lms.ac.uk/about/council/lms-elections LMS Election Results 2019]</ref>

He was Head of School of Mathematics at the University of Edinburgh between 2014 and 2021, at which point he was succeeded by Prof 
Bernd J Schroers. Gordon has been Vice-Principal and Head of the College of Science and Engineering at the [[University of Edinburgh]] since 2021. As Vice-Principal, Gordon is a member of the Senior Leadership Team and University Executive.<ref>https://principals-office.ed.ac.uk/senior-leadership-team</ref><ref>https://governance-strategic-planning.ed.ac.uk/governance/university-committees/othercommitteesandgroups/university-executive/membership</ref> On 20 May 2025, the Senate, the University of Edinburgh's supreme academic body, approved the motion that "Senate has no confidence in the University Executive’s leadership in relation to the University’s financial situation", by a two thirds majority.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://registryservices.ed.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2025-05/20%20May%202025%20-%20Agenda%20and%20Papers_1.pdf | title=Financial Resilience Strategy Update and Confidence in the University Executive | page=118 | website=registryservices.ed.ac.uk}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cm266dn4qljo | title=Edinburgh University staff back strike action over £140m cuts | date=21 May 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://news.stv.tv/east-central/edinburgh-university-staff-back-strike-action-over-140m-cuts-and-threat-to-jobs | title=Edinburgh University staff back strike action over £140m cuts | date=21 May 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.parliament.scot/chamber-and-committees/official-report/search-what-was-said-in-parliament/lghp-04-06-2025?meeting=16488 | title=Education, Children and Young People Committee | date=2025-06-04 | page=39}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Iain Gordon has two children with Dr Maja Waldhausen,<ref>{{Cite news |date=2021-05-21 |title=The 10-year-old boy who beat a chess grandmaster - but didn't want to boast |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-edinburgh-east-fife-57187522 |access-date=2026-07-25 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref> daughter of mathematician [[Friedhelm Waldhausen]]; Josephine Waldhausen Gordon (born 2010) and [[Frederick Waldhausen Gordon]] (born 2012).<ref>{{Cite web |title=PhDs and post-docs and anothers |url=https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~igordon/phdstudents.html |access-date=2026-07-25 |website=webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk}}</ref>
